identity.trade: Charcoal and smelting: Cindermoor's kilns burn the moorland oak that feeds the vale's forges.

greeting: Boss here. Short for the one who gets blamed.
Welcome to Cindermoor. Mind the Cindermoor Kilns. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: A seam we mapped does not match the rock. Somebody moved the markers.
Pay day was delayed and nobody complained. When miners stop complaining, worry.
Smoke on the moor after dusk is ours. If you can't smell it, it is not.

opinions.maeve_swale: I would trust Maeve with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: Shift is up. Bring a lamp, bring a prayer.

dialogue.aside: Welcome, welcome. Your name is right there. On the tip of my tongue.

greeting: Ale is fair, stew is hot, and I do not do credit.
Cindermoor is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Miners drink quick and tip slow. I water the first and ignore the second.
Somebody paid in old coin last night. Very old. Nobody knew the king on it.
The pit ponies shy at the same turning every shift. The foreman has stopped using that turning.
Charcoal costs more this year: someone is cutting trees beyond the ward.

opinions.greta_crowther: Greta has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Greta.

time.evening: Shift is done. Wash the dust off, if the water allows.

dialogue.aside: Mind the order of things, friend. There. Now we can talk.

greeting: Mind the anvil. It has opinions.
Cindermoor is charcoal burners. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Picks wear out in a week and wedges in a day. I keep a pile ready.
Hinges, hooks, wolf-bells. That is what sells now.
The rock dust has a taste lately. Sweet, like iron and old pennies.

opinions.gunnar_lyle: Gunnar has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Gunnar.
opinions.maeve_swale: Maeve lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.night: Night shift. Keep your voice low. The rock listens.

dialogue.aside: My friend. Come, I kept something for you. A small thing. It means a lot to me.

greeting: If it is not on the shelf, I can find it. If it cannot be found, I can find you something similar.
Lamp up and mind the timber. We say it twice and mean it.
rumour: Candles, picks, tallow. Everything is bought by the dozen and burned by dusk.
Folk buy more than they need, then bring half back. Fear shops strangely.
A lamp flame leaned sideways in a sealed gallery. There is a draught from somewhere with no door.
Whatever you hear about Cindermoor, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.greta_crowther: Greta keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.wystan_seam: Wystan is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.rain: Rain. The pit floods and the pumps groan. Everybody bails.

dialogue.aside: Punctual as ever, friend. I admire that. I also resent it.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
Folk come to Cindermoor for charcoal burners. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: The old stones had names. Nobody writes them down. Nobody asks me.
Pit props are failing on the third level. The foreman says rot. The crew says a knock.
Dov Sutt swears the old moor road has a stone nobody carved.

opinions.vera_nettle: I would trust Vera with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: Shift is up. Bring a lamp, bring a prayer.

dialogue.aside: A bright day and a bright friend! What luck!

greeting: Do not breathe near the kiln. Or do. I am not your mother.
First time in Cindermoor? The Cindermoor Kilns is the place to start.
rumour: The far kiln was cold when I woke. No fire, no ash, no scorch on the ground.
The mine cat will not go below the second level. He is the best judge of air we have.

opinions.lyle_winslow: Lyle knows the trade. I will say that for Lyle.
opinions.nial_lathom: Nial lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.evening: Shift is done. Wash the dust off, if the water allows.

dialogue.aside: Ha! Friend! Pull up a stool, I have a story and half a loaf.

greeting: Lamp up, helmet down. We talk later.
The Cindermoor Kilns is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: The north shaft is shut again. The foreman says the roof. The miners say not.
The deepest miner swears the rock breathes. He is not drunk, which is the worrying part.

opinions.letty_ledger: Letty lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.lorne_hurst: Lorne keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.night: Night shift. Keep your voice low. The rock listens.

dialogue.aside: Knock on wood, friend. Now touch iron. There. Safe, for a while.

greeting: Coal dust never leaves. Not the lungs, not the stew.
Dust is the town's second weather. Mind your lungs.
rumour: A tunnel we closed in spring was open this morning. Nobody dug it.
A new shaft hit water and nobody could stop it. The water was warm.
If trade slows, Cindermoor feels it first. If it speeds up, Cindermoor feels it last.

opinions.brida_thackeray: Brida works hard and talks harder.
opinions.nial_lathom: Nial keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.rain: Rain. The pit floods and the pumps groan. Everybody bails.

dialogue.aside: Sit. I have news. Three pieces, one of them true, I think.

greeting: Hands on the belt. Not that one. That one bites.
You will hear Cindermoor before you see it. Ask at the Cindermoor Kilns.
rumour: A lump rang like a bell when I dropped it. Rang for a minute. Dull lead, I told the foreman.
The ore carts run late. The road is fine. The carters are afraid.

opinions.letty_ledger: Letty works hard and talks harder.
opinions.madoc_sheaf: Madoc knows the trade. I will say that for Madoc.

time.morning: Shift is up. Bring a lamp, bring a prayer.

dialogue.aside: Peace to you, friend. The day opens like a book. Sit and read with me.

greeting: Stand back from the heat. It does not like being looked at.
You look clean. Give it an hour.
rumour: The furnace draws like a bellows even when the bellows rest. I check the flue twice a day.
Strange scratches on the tunnel wall, above head height. We stopped the dig.
A stranger asked at the Cindermoor Kilns for the oldest person in Cindermoor. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.derwin_pargeter: Derwin works hard and talks harder.
opinions.lyle_winslow: Lyle knows the trade. I will say that for Lyle.

time.evening: Shift is done. Wash the dust off, if the water allows.

dialogue.aside: You look tired, friend. I will not lie. Rest.

greeting: Hold the mule. He is not as bad as he looks.
Strangers in Cindermoor get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Toll at the ford has gone up. So has my temper.
Every few years Cindermoor has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.esmer_forrest: Esmer knows the trade. I will say that for Esmer.
opinions.lyle_winslow: Lyle works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Night shift. Keep your voice low. The rock listens.

dialogue.aside: Whatever you need, friend. Ask. I will not make you ask twice.

greeting: My back says no. My purse says yes.
rumour: Hands wanted everywhere and nobody pays for hands.
The Cindermoor Kilns has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

opinions.derwin_pargeter: Derwin lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.esmer_forrest: Esmer knows the trade. I will say that for Esmer.

time.rain: Rain. The pit floods and the pumps groan. Everybody bails.

dialogue.aside: I dreamed of you last night. You were a heron. It suited you.

greeting: Mind the lamp. Mind the roof. Mind me.
rumour: The roof sang at dawn, a low note. Everyone stopped. Then everyone went back to work.
Folk say Cindermoor was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.derwin_pargeter: Derwin knows the trade. I will say that for Derwin.
opinions.esmer_forrest: Esmer works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Shift is up. Bring a lamp, bring a prayer.

dialogue.aside: Up before dawn, friend? Then you saw the best of the day. I saw it first.

greeting: Coal dust never leaves. Not the lungs, not the stew.
rumour: Something knocks back when you knock on the deep face.
The Cindermoor Kilns was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.brida_thackeray: Brida works hard and talks harder.
opinions.vera_nettle: Vera keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.evening: Shift is done. Wash the dust off, if the water allows.

dialogue.aside: Hello. A pause. I am glad you came. That is all.

greeting: Mind the lamp. Mind the roof. Mind me.
rumour: Ask in Cindermoor who built the Cindermoor Kilns and you will get a different name each time.
When Cindermoor is quiet we say it is peaceful. When it is very quiet we say nothing.

opinions.kit_ingleby: I would trust Kit with a purse. A small one.
opinions.lyle_winslow: Lyle works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Night shift. Keep your voice low. The rock listens.

dialogue.aside: Tell me everything. No, truly. I will not ask twice. I will ask three times.

greeting: Do you have a dog? I do not have a dog. Yet.
rumour: I saw a light in the hedge last night. Do not tell Mum.
The mine cat will not go below the second level. He is the best judge of air we have.

opinions.sunniva_vickery: Sunniva is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

clues.note: A survey stone sits a hand's width from its mark. The old socket is clean.
A pit prop charred at the foot. Someone lit a small fire and stamped it out.
A chain cut clean with a good tool and wrapped to look whole.

stashes.say: You carry four split logs from the stack.
You fill a sack with four lumps of good ore.
